## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column must be fixed before merge: it returns the timestamp of a `started` event, so every non-NULL value is a start time published as a finish time. Its documented NULL meaning is also wrong for a process that started and was later cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — finished_at returns the 'started' event timestamp — For process 20, whose latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, `finished_at` returns that start time although the process has not finished. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no event marks a finish, while `models/schema.yml:11` documents "Timestamp when the process finished." — Consumers read a start time as a completion time and treat running processes as finished. — Fix: Either rename the column and its description to `started_at`, or derive it from the event that marks completion; the source table defines no `finished` event, so the code cannot settle which is intended.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL meaning documented for finished_at — For process 30 (`started`, then `cleared`), the column is NULL, yet the description says "NULL means the process has never been started." The expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` reads only the latest event, so any later event nulls the value. — Consumers who filter on NULL to find never-started processes also get processes that started and were later cleared.
